incidents.victim: LaLiga and affiliated Spanish football clubs
incidents.vector: Hackers compromised a technology platform used by amateur football clubs affiliated with the Spanish football league.
incidents.impact: User data was stolen from the platform.

incidents.victim: CIA and Office of the Director of National Intelligence
incidents.vector: Hackers breached an IT system supporting an open-source intelligence (OSINT) analysis platform shared by the two agencies.
incidents.impact: Exposed unclassified data; officials say classified networks and information were not involved and no other systems are currently at risk.

incidents.vector: Attackers exploited CVE-2026-134624, a server-side request forgery flaw, to breach an N-able server hosting the Mail Assure and SpamExperts email security platform.
incidents.impact: Caused roughly a week of outages to Mail Assure dashboards; N-able found no evidence of exploitation beyond the single compromised server after remediation.

incidents.victim: Microsoft Entra Connect Health customers (multiple tenants)
incidents.vector: A security flaw in the Microsoft Entra Connect Health API allowed unauthorized read-only access to tenant metadata.
incidents.impact: Multiple organizations received Microsoft security notifications confirming unauthorized access to tenant contact and configuration metadata; some notified tenants report they do not even use the affected service.

incidents.vector: Attacker used a cloud access key Barracuda had issued to a third-party AI service provider and failed to revoke, then deployed the ARTEX agentic AI penetration-testing framework to escalate access across internal and cloud environments.
incidents.impact: Threat actor accessed Barracuda's cloud environment for nearly two days before being detected and evicted.

incidents.vector: An unauthorized third party gained access to a database tied to the McDonald's Japan mobile app, apparently using stolen authentication credentials.
incidents.impact: Exposed customer purchase histories, IP addresses, internal customer IDs and mobile device location data; names, payment data and contact details were not affected.

incidents.vector: Hackers accessed application code, databases, and API and integration keys for customer environments.
incidents.impact: Company replaced its entire cloud environment in response; expects to lose $2.5 million as a result of the incident.

incidents.vector: An internal API belonging to Radware was accidentally exposed to the internet and scraped by attackers.
incidents.impact: Customer contact details and, in some cases, credentials used for cloud log storage were stolen; affected customers advised to rotate compromised credentials.

incidents.vector: Not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Customer data was stolen in a security breach; the utility issued a public apology.

incidents.victim: Chinese identity verification database (exposed Elasticsearch instance)
incidents.vector: A misconfigured Elasticsearch database was left exposed on the internet without authentication.
incidents.impact: More than 1.6 billion records covering over 840 million individuals leaked, including names, national ID numbers, mobile numbers, school enrollment and business registration data, apparently sourced from an underground commercial data-lookup service.

incidents.victim: T-Mobile, Cisco, Fujitsu, Quintel and CNEX (Huawei trade secret theft)
incidents.vector: Huawei employees and proxies violated non-disclosure agreements and used corporate espionage — including smuggling a T-Mobile testing robot component, copying Cisco router source code, and using a recruited university researcher as a proxy against CNEX — to steal proprietary U.S. technology over roughly two decades.
incidents.impact: A federal jury convicted Huawei Technologies and three subsidiaries of conspiracy to steal trade secrets, bank and wire fraud, Iran sanctions violations, and money laundering; sentencing is set for Sept. 14, 2027.

incidents.vector: AI agents built on the Cairn penetration-testing framework autonomously discovered and exploited a zero-day path-traversal flaw in an exposed open-source medical imaging application, reaching root access in about 11 minutes.
incidents.impact: Attacker gained full control of a university server during a roughly 48-hour campaign that also included extensive unsuccessful attempts against an exposed Redis instance and a GPU server.

incidents.vector: North Korean cyber actors stole more than $6 billion in cryptocurrency from Binance on or about Oct. 29, 2026.
incidents.impact: DOJ filed a civil action to forfeit over $1.1 billion in laundered USDC proceeds; roughly $2.9 billion in stolen assets has been frozen, seized or returned to date through coordination with Binance and industry partners.

incidents.vector: An unidentified threat actor exploited a flaw in the Classic tier of Microsoft Azure API Management to access stored credentials and other sensitive tokens.
incidents.impact: Equinor detected the intrusion and fully contained it by Nov. 20; some internal services were disrupted but oil and gas production was unaffected. Skagerak Energi was also affected, with no indication of data compromise at either company.

incidents.vector: Attackers breached Wagyu's web hosting provider, 1984 Hosting, and stole a developer access key from old server logs.
incidents.impact: $13.5 million worth of tokens stolen from Wagyu; the underlying hosting-provider breach also knocked more than 20,000 other websites offline.

incidents.victim: ~80 major US newspapers (including Boston Herald, Denver Post, Newsday, New York Daily News, Mercury News)
incidents.vector: A Magecart-style web skimmer hidden inside a shared Naviga subscription payment widget used WebRTC to stream entered payment card data live to attacker infrastructure, bypassing the need for a form submission.
incidents.impact: The malicious script loaded roughly 15,000 times per day across the affected subscription payment pages, capturing card data entered directly into forms; users who paid via Apple Pay, Google Pay or PayPal were not affected.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached the online share-trading division's customer support system.
incidents.impact: Personal data of more than 8,000 clients stolen, including names, mailing addresses and ID scans.

incidents.victim: Instituto da Mobilidade e dos Transportes / ADENE (Portugal energy agency)
incidents.vector: Not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Portugal's energy agency suspended its energy certification platform following the weekend cyberattack.

incidents.vector: Not disclosed.
incidents.impact: The German web hosting provider was breached; the company reset all customer passwords over the weekend to evict the attacker from customer systems.

incidents.vector: A threat actor gained access to WP connect's infrastructure and injected malware into six of its WordPress plugins.
incidents.impact: The compromised plugins deployed a backdoor for several hours before WordPress.org permanently removed them; site owners must still manually remove the backdoor.

incidents.victim: Federal Bureau of Investigation (National Crime Information Center)
incidents.vector: Hackers breached the FBI's National Crime Information Center, a national database used for warrants, fugitives, missing persons and background checks.
incidents.impact: Second breach at the FBI in recent months (following a September incident tied to ShinyHunters); FBI Director Kash Patel confirmed an active investigation but declined to disclose what data was accessed.

incidents.vector: Attackers gained access to one of the cross-chain exchange's vault keys.
incidents.impact: $12 million in assets stolen and laundered through the Tornado Cash mixing service; the platform suspended operations and its token lost roughly a third of its value.

incidents.vector: Attackers breached the platform's bridge connecting to its ACE token.
incidents.impact: $5.7 million in assets stolen from the platform.

incidents.victim: GL.iNet customers (travel routers, IP KVM devices)
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in GL.iNet's GoodCloud remote-access service to connect to customer devices and install backdoors disguised as a cron process.
incidents.impact: An unknown number of travel routers and IP KVM devices were backdoored; GL.iNet shipped patched firmware and recommends a factory reset for infected units.

incidents.vector: Threat actors impersonated Mr. Cooper employees in phone calls to the company's IT help desk to fraudulently obtain temporary passwords, bypassing multi-factor authentication controls.
incidents.impact: Large amounts of private customer information were stolen in a November 2023 breach; NYDFS fined Rocket Mortgage, which later acquired Mr. Cooper, $6.75 million for related cybersecurity control failures, including untimely incident reporting and inadequate MFA.

incidents.vector: Webworm (also tracked as Erudite Mogwai / Space Pirates) deploys a customized, obfuscated build of SoftEther VPN disguised as "NtMonitor" network-monitoring software to maintain stealthy long-term access to compromised networks.
incidents.impact: Long-term unauthorized remote access maintained on previously compromised European government networks; researchers attribute the tool to Webworm with moderate confidence.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached the myColorado mobile app, used by 2.1 million residents for digital identification, document storage and state services.
incidents.impact: The app was taken offline; the state believes data on nearly 150,000 people was stolen, though the exact data types have not been disclosed.

incidents.victim: Cryptocurrency holders, gaming platform users and VoIP software users in Europe
incidents.vector: Trojanized lure files — fake financial-statement PDFs and VoIP softphone installers — deliver the Go-based Overlord RAT and a Python infostealer via weaponized LNK, HTA and MSBuild living-off-the-land techniques.
incidents.impact: Credential, cryptocurrency-wallet and clipboard-hijacking malware deployed against victims across Europe; Talos assesses with low confidence that the campaign, tracked as UAT-12643, is North Korea-aligned based on shared RAT and blockchain C2 infrastructure.

incidents.victim: 178+ websites, including BBC, CNN, Equifax, Ledger and Zoom
incidents.vector: An attacker exploited CVE-2026-132224 in Optimizely Web Experimentation to inject malicious JavaScript into customer A/B-testing scripts loaded on affected websites.
incidents.impact: 178 websites briefly served data-stealing malware and iOS zero-click exploit kits to visitors; researchers estimate roughly $7,500 in cryptocurrency was stolen along with an unknown number of payment card records.

incidents.victim: Multiple organizations worldwide (365+ claimed in Q3 2026)
incidents.vector: Qilin ransomware-as-a-service affiliates compromise victim networks and deploy double-extortion ransomware, stealing data before encrypting systems and threatening to publish it.
incidents.impact: Qilin has become the world's most active ransomware affiliate program, claiming at least 365 victim organizations in the past three months; researchers identified the group's administrator as a St. Petersburg, Russia-based individual.

incidents.vector: A hacker breached payments processor Cleverbridge and stole payment card data.
incidents.impact: The company is notifying affected customers and asking them to monitor card statements for fraudulent activity.
